summary: The port reproduces the automaton itself essentially exactly (per-pixel field matches the original within +/-1 at every dialed setting tested), but it skips the original's progressive top-down build-up, walks its ~32.7 s colour cycle at a constant rate where the original's is strongly non-uniform, and starts from a different (randomised) seed row when no controls are touched.
observations: Rig: 16x16 grid, 256 px. Both sides compile and run clean (no compileError/runtimeError), neither binds sensors (wantsSensors false on both).

Control surface is identical: both sides expose sliderParam/Param, sliderPan/Pan, sliderDepth/Depth, sliderElimStripes/ElimStripes, sliderRandomSeeds/RandomSeeds, all kind 'slider'. probe.json marks all five responsive on both sides (orig maxDeltaLit 27-36, port 45-53).

The pattern is a one-shot automaton, not a continuously animating one: after the first ~1-2 s the 16x16 field is FROZEN on both sides and the only ongoing motion is a global colour cycle. Confirmed over 200 s (label longcycle) and in late windows at t=90-110 s (late-dialed) and t=120-150 s (late-untouched) - neither side dies, freezes black, or saturates. survey statsSummary motion avg 1.1 on both; zeroMotionFrames is high purely because the field is static.

Automaton accuracy is excellent. At sliderParam=0.1 with the other four dialed to 0.5, a --dump at t=8 s gives per-pixel max-channel fields that agree cell-for-cell within +/-1 across all 256 pixels (orig mean 103.3, port mean 103.5) - label par01-dump. The same holds at Param 0.5 (dial-mid-dump: green channel identical to within 1-2 everywhere).

Param selects distinct automaton textures and both sides land on the SAME texture at the same value: 0.1/0.2 = repeated bracket lattice, 0.35 = similar lattice, 0.5 = plain horizontal bands, 0.65 = wavy arch lattice, 0.8 = sparse bands. Param exactly 0 and exactly 1 render fully black on BOTH sides; 0.05 and 0.95 are alive on both.

BUILD-UP DIVERGENCE: untouched, the original starts with a single lit pixel in row 0 (col 8, RGB 254,219,0) and propagates roughly one generation per frame downward - deepest lit row is 0 at frame 0, 2 at frame 1, 6 at frame 5, 11 at frame 10, 15 at frame 15 (label fill-dump, 20 fps). The port has ALL 16 rows already populated at frame 0 and only fades up in brightness. Same at dialed settings (fill-dump-mid): the original's row values march downward and reach row 15 around frame 30-40 while the port's whole field is present from frame 0.

The build-up onset is frame-stepped on both sides and consistently offset: at Param/Pan/Depth/Elim/Seeds all 0.5, orig meanBrightness first exceeds 0 at frame 12 at 10, 20 and 40 fps; the port at frame 2 at all three rates (labels ramp-10/ramp-20/ramp-40). So the port reaches a lit field ~10 frames (0.5 s at 20 fps) earlier and shows no growth animation.

COLOUR-CYCLE DIVERGENCE: both sides cycle the whole field through the full hue circle with an identical period - autocorrelation of meanR over a 200 s / 3 fps run gives a first peak at lag 98 frames = 32.67 s on BOTH sides. But the port advances hue at a CONSTANT rate (measured on a fixed pixel at dial-mid: 21.9 deg per 2 s at every sample from t=4 to t=38, label dial-mid-hue2), while the original's rate varies roughly 8x over the cycle - about 2 deg/s while it sits on red (hue near 0, t=26-31) rising to about 17 deg/s through cyan/blue (hue 180-240, t=44-50 in the survey). The original visibly lingers on red/orange and races through cyan/blue; the port sweeps evenly.

Consequence of that: the two sides drift apart and re-converge once per 33 s cycle. Mean-frame hue on the untouched survey: t=11 s orig 133.0 / port 133.0 (identical), t=23 s orig 317.0 / port 264.8 (52 deg apart, orig magenta vs port blue-violet), t=32 s orig 5.1 / port 4.5 (identical again), t=38 s orig 48.2 / port 70.3. Contact sheets show it as the port reading yellow-green where the original reads orange (ctl-Param-0.2, ctl-Param-0.65 at t=1.1-5.4 s).

The within-frame hue spread differs the same way: at dial-mid t=8 s the original's darkest-to-brightest cell spans hue 121.8 -> 78.9 deg (43 deg) while the port spans 147.4 -> 119.5 (28 deg); across the cycle the original's spread swings between about 4 and 27 deg per sample while the port's is pinned at 29 deg. Direction of the shift (hue decreases as cell value rises) is the same on both.

UNTOUCHED-DEFAULT DIVERGENCE: with no controls applied the original seeds a single centre cell and grows one symmetric centred pyramid figure; the port starts from a fully populated, randomised-looking top row (6-12 lit cells in row 0 at frame 0) and settles into a repeated bracket/tile texture spanning the grid - essentially what the original looks like at Param around 0.2. Visible in baseline, survey and late-untouched sheets and confirmed by --dump at t=8 s (untouched-dump). Untouched meanBrightness avg 37 (orig) vs 55 (port) over the 60 s survey.

The untouched divergence tracks sliderParam, not sliderRandomSeeds: with ONLY sliderRandomSeeds=0 set (label seedsonly-0) the original still seeds one pixel while the port still seeds a full random row, but with ONLY sliderParam=0.5 set the port collapses to a single central seed hump. With all four other sliders set and RandomSeeds left untouched (label noseeds) both sides seed identically.

Once ANY full set of dial values is applied the two sides agree on brightness as well: dial-mid orig/port meanBrightness avg 16.1/17.3 with identical min 0 / max 25 / last 25; ctl-Depth-0 18.4/18.4; ctl-Pan-0 15.3/16.6. The larger untouched brightness gap is a consequence of the different seed row, not of different output amplitude - the per-pixel value fields match exactly (see par01-dump).

SEED FRAGILITY: at sliderRandomSeeds=1 the port's randomised field occasionally collapses. Mean per-row lateral standard deviation of luma at t=8 s across seeds 1, 2, 7, 42, 99, 500, 1234, 7777 - orig 56.4, 59.8, 48.6, 76.7, 73.3, 64.6, 57.8, 74.4 (always richly varied); port 62.0, 61.7, 50.5, 61.8, 63.7, 42.2, 10.9, 57.0. At seed 1234 the port renders plain uniform horizontal bands with almost no lateral variation while the original is fully mottled (labels seed1234-rs1, sd1234).

sliderElimStripes behaves identically on both sides including its failure mode: no visible change between 0 and 0.5, then the output is completely black at 0.55, 0.6, 0.65, 0.7, 0.75, 0.9 and 1 on BOTH sides.

dials.name: sliderParam
dials.origEffect: Selects the automaton rule. Black at exactly 0 and exactly 1; alive from 0.05 to 0.95, each value producing a distinct frozen texture (0.1/0.2 repeated bracket lattice, 0.5 plain horizontal bands, 0.65 wavy arch lattice, 0.8 sparse bands). Field brightness falls from mean ~40 at 0.1-0.2 to ~13 at 0.95.
dials.portEffect: Same textures at the same values, same black-out at exactly 0 and 1. At Param=0.1 the per-pixel field matches the original cell-for-cell within +/-1. Only difference is the port renders it ~10 frames earlier and in a slightly different hue.

dials.name: sliderPan
dials.origEffect: Subtle re-phasing of the field. 0 and 1 render identically to each other (same stats: mb avg 15.3, max 24, last 23); 0.25 and 0.75 give a slightly dimmer, more open banding (mb avg 13).
dials.portEffect: Identical behaviour and identical wrap: Pan 0 and Pan 1 byte-equal in stats on the port too (mb avg 16.6 both), 0.25/0.75 dimmer (14) with the same visible banding as the original.

dials.name: sliderDepth
dials.origEffect: Widens the seed row and dims the field as it rises: mb avg 18.4 at 0, 17 at 0.25, 16.1 at 0.5, 15 at 0.75, 14.1 at 1; the seed row goes from 1 lit cell to a ~9-cell hump.
dials.portEffect: Same direction and same structures (18.4 at 0, 18 at 0.25, 17.3 at 0.5, 17 at 0.75, 17 at 1). The port's dimming with Depth is slightly weaker than the original's (orig loses ~23% brightness from 0 to 1, port ~8%).

dials.name: sliderElimStripes
dials.origEffect: No visible change from 0 to 0.5 (0 and 0.5 give identical stats); at 0.55 and above the output goes fully black and stays black through 1.
dials.portEffect: Identical - same no-op below 0.5, same hard black-out threshold between 0.5 and 0.55, black through 1. Effect below the threshold is not visible in output on either side, so the intended 'eliminate stripes' behaviour is unverifiable from renders on both.

dials.name: sliderRandomSeeds
dials.origEffect: At 0 and 0.5 the top row is a single centred seed (1 lit cell at 0, a symmetric 7-cell hump at 0.5) producing a symmetric figure; at 1 the top row is randomised, producing a mottled vertical-stripe texture (mb avg 38 vs 16 at 0.5). Randomised result is richly varied on all 8 seeds tested.
dials.portEffect: At 0.5 and 1 with the other four dials set, matches the original (single centred hump at 0.5; mottled randomised texture at 1, mb 40.8 vs orig 38.1). Two gaps: (a) with ONLY this slider set to 0 the port still seeds a full random row where the original seeds one pixel; (b) at seed 1234 the port's randomised field collapses to near-uniform horizontal bands (row std 10.9 vs the original's 57.8).

feedback: Restore the progressive build-up. The original reveals the automaton one generation per frame downward from the seed row - deepest lit row goes 0, 2, 6, 11, 15 at frames 0, 1, 5, 10, 15 - and does not show a lit pixel at all until frame 12 (frame-counted, identical at 10/20/40 fps). The port has all 16 rows populated at frame 0 and only fades in brightness, so the first second of the pattern reads as a cross-fade instead of a growing automaton. Match the original's onset delay (~12 frames of black) and its one-row-per-frame reveal.

Fix the colour-cycle traversal. Both sides cycle the whole field through the hue circle in the same 32.67 s (autocorrelation first peak, lag 98 frames at 3 fps, both sides). The port advances hue at a constant 21.9 deg per 2 s. The original does NOT: it crawls at about 2 deg/s while sitting on red (hue near 0) and accelerates to about 17 deg/s through cyan/blue (hue 180-240), an ~8x swing per cycle, so the original visibly dwells on red/orange and rushes through the blues. Result is up to 52 deg of hue disagreement mid-cycle (survey t=23 s: orig mean hue 317 deg magenta, port 265 deg blue-violet) with the two coinciding twice a cycle (t=11 s and t=32 s). Replace the port's linear hue ramp with the original's non-uniform colour map; the total period is already right.

The same non-uniformity governs the within-frame value-to-hue spread: at dial-mid the original's darkest-to-brightest cells span 43 deg of hue at t=8 s but only ~4 deg when the cycle is parked on red, while the port always spans a fixed ~29 deg. Whatever fixes the temporal traversal should make the spatial spread breathe with it too.

Untouched (no control values applied) the port's initial state differs from the original's: the original seeds one centre pixel in row 0 and grows a single symmetric pyramid, the port seeds a fully populated randomised top row and settles into a repeated bracket lattice (roughly the original's Param=0.2 look). The trigger is sliderParam's internal default, not sliderRandomSeeds - setting only sliderParam=0.5 on the port restores a single central seed, while setting only sliderRandomSeeds=0 does not. Make the port's top-level default for the Param global match whatever the original assigns, so a freshly loaded pattern shows the same figure.

sliderRandomSeeds=1 is not robust to the RNG stream on the port. Across seeds 1, 2, 7, 42, 99, 500, 1234, 7777 the original's randomised field always has strong lateral variation (per-row luma std 48.6-76.7); the port's ranges 10.9-63.7 and at seed 1234 collapses to almost uniform horizontal bands (std 10.9). Something in the port's seed generation can degenerate to a near-constant row - widen or re-scale the random seed values so the field stays mottled for every seed.

No fidelity work needed on the automaton itself: at sliderParam=0.1 (others 0.5) the two sides' per-pixel value fields agree within +/-1 across all 256 pixels, and the same holds at Param 0.5. Param, Pan, Depth and ElimStripes all reproduce the original's response including the exact ElimStripes black-out threshold between 0.5 and 0.55 and Param's black-out at exactly 0 and 1. Do not touch those.
